items.title: Manuel Joseph "Moose" Zanco Interview, 1959-11-25
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Johnny Lane; the interviewer introduces Johnny Lane as a separate anecdote about reading Shakespeare, which the interviewee does not directly address or confirm knowledge of.

ctx.x: Uh, incidentally, uh, Joe, Joe was a great, uh, Shakespearean fan, you know? Joe read Shakespeare every night of his life, man. And, I think when he graduated from high school, his mother had given him a, uh, oh, I think comedy tragedy and something or else, you know, all about Shakespeare. And, uh, it got to be like a tonic with him. Uh, you might say a, a sleep inducer. He had to read a few lines of Shakespeare every night before he went to sleep, you know? And, I mean, it was things like that that made a…

Well, Johnny Lane is the same. He sits up on the stand. This is a guy from Chicago that studied under Jimmy Newman. He sits up on the stand. On the stand. He might have had it right the first time. But anyways, he sits on the stand and reads Shakespeare, you know, between numbers. And Joe's Boonies will be playing with him. And he'll say, well, the next number is dedicated to our boss. High psychiatry. You know?

Well, I tell you, I've seen, uh, I've seen Archie Rogers in between numbers almost go to sleep on the bandstand. He'll, to me, he actually looks like he dozes. And on the next tune, he's as live as can be.
